records.description: NATURE OF THE CASE ALLIED CHEMICAL OWNED AND OPERATED THE BATON ROUGE EDC/VCM FACILITY UNTIL SEPTEMBER 14, 1978, AT WHICH TIME THE PLANT WAS SOLD TO ICI AMERICAS, INC. THE PLANT WAS THEN SOLD ON JANUARY 1, 1981, BY ICI TO FORMOSA PLASTICS CORPORATION LOUISIANA, WHICH IS THE PRESENT OWNER OF THE PLANT. FROM AUGUST 12, 1978, TO THE PRESENT DATE, 23 DIS- CHARGES HAVE BEEN REPORTED AS EMERGENCIES FOR A TOTAL OF MORE THAN 47,080 POUNDS OF VC FROM THE EDC/VCM PLANT. ONE DISCHARGE OCCURRED WHILE UNDER ALLIED'S OWNERSHIP, 15 WHILE UNDER ICI'S OWNERSHIP, AND 7 UNDER FORMOSA'S OWNERSHIP. EMISSIONS FROM THE EDC/VCM FACILITY ARE SUBJECT TO THE NATIONAL EMISSIONS STANDARDS FOR HAZARDOUS AIR POLLUTANTS (NESHAP), 40 CFR PART 61. CIVIL SUIT FOR PENALTIES AND IN- JUNCTIVE RELIEF AGAINST THE PRESENT OWNER FORMOSA AND FOR PENALTIES ONLY AGAINST THE FORMER OWNER ICI IS REQUESTED PURSUANT TO SECTION 113(B)(3) OF THE CLEAN AIR ACT. CAUSE OF ACTION THE NATIONAL EMISSION STANDARD FOR VINYL CHLORIDE, 40 CFR 61.60 ET SEQ. WAS PROMULGATED OCTOBER 21, 1976. AMONG OTHER THINGS, THE REGULATIONS PROHIBIT VINYL CHLORIDE (VC) DISCHARGES FROM ANY RELIEF VALVE IN VC SERVICE EXCEPT FOR EMERGENCIES; REQUIRE REPORTING OF RELIEF VALVE DISCHARGES WITHIN 10 DAYS; LIMIT VC EMISSIONS FROM EQUIPMENT USED IN EDC PURIFICATION AND IN VC FORMATION AND PURIFICATION TO 10 PPM, VC EMISSIONS REMOVED FROM IN PROCESS WASTEWATER AND\ DUCTED THROUGH A CONTROL SYSTEM. REGION 6 FIRST INITIATED INVESTIGATION OF 22 DISCHARGES REPORTED FOR THE BATON ROUGE, LOUISIANA FACILITY BY ISSUING A LETTER UNDER SECTION 114 OF THE CLEAN AIR ACT, DATED JUNE 18, 1982. (ONE ADDITIONAL DISCHARGE OCCURRED AFTER THIS DATE.) THIS LETTER WAS SENT IN ORDER TO OBTAIN ADDITIONAL INFORMATION ON EACH DISCHARGE FOR THE PURPOSE OF DETERMINING PREVENTABILITY AND COMPLIANCE. FORMOSA AND THE TWO PREVIOUS OWNERS RESPONDED SEPARATELY FOR DISCHARGES UNDER THEIR RE- SPECTIVE OWNERSHIPS; FORMOSA BY LETTER HAND-DELIVERED ON ON AUGUST 26, 1982, ICI BY LETTER DATED DECEMBER 2, 1982, AND ALLIED BY LETTER DATED AUGUST 26, 1982. OF THE 23 REPORTED DISCHARGES, EIGHT (8) DISCHARGES (TOTALLING 23,854 LBS) MAY BE CONSIDERED NON-EMERGENCY OR VIOLATIONS OF 40 CFR 61.65(A) UNDER CONDITIONS OF PREVENT- ABLE OPERATOR ERROR AND PREVENTABLE EQUIPMENT FAILURE. FOUR (4) DISCHARGES TOTALLING 369 LBS. MAY BE CONSIDERED VIOLA- TIONS OF 40 CFR 61.62(A), THE 10 PPM VC STANDARD FOR EDC PURIFICATION AND SEVEN (7) DISCHARGES TOTALLING 22,855 LBS. MAY BE CONSIDERED VIOLATIONS OF 40 CFR 61.63(A), THE 10 PPM VC STANDARD FOR VC FORMATION AND PURIFICATION. TWO (2) DIS- CHARGES OF UNKNOWN QUANTITIES OF VC MAY BE CONSIDERED VIOLA- TIONS OF BOTH 40 CFR 61.62(A) AND 61.63(A); AND, TWO (2) DISCHARGES TOTALLING 2 LBS. WHICH WERE SUBJECT TO 40 CFR 61.63(A) WERE DETERMINED TO BE IN COMPLIANCE WITH THAT STAND DARD.

records.description: 1. SECTION 3008(A) OF THE SOLID WASTE DISPOSAL ACT, AS A- MEMDED BY THE RESOURCE CONSERVATION AND RECOVERY ACT AND THE HAZARDOUS AND SOLID WASTE AMENDMENTS OF 1984, 42 U.S.C. SEC. 6901 ET. SEQ. ( RCRA ). 2. FORMOSA PLASTICS CORPORATION P.O. BOX 400 POINT COMFORT, TEXAS 77978 FACILITY ID NO. TXT490011293 3. RESPONDENT HAS VIOLATED THE REGULATIONS OF SUBTITLE C OF RCRA BY COUNT 1: FAILURE TO SUBMIT A PART A AND PART B PERMIT, COUNT 2: FAILURE TO PREPARE AND FOLLOW A WASTE PLAN ANALYSIS, COUNT 3: FAILURE TO MAKE AN ADEQUATE HAZ- ARDOUS WASTE DETERMINATION, COUNT 4: FAILURE TO USE AND MAINTAIN CONTAINERS WHICH ARE STURDY, LEAKPROOF AND WILL NOT BE DETERIORATED BY THEIR CONTENTS AND ARE OF SUFFI- CIENT STRENGTH AND CONSTRUCTION, COUNT 5: FAILURE TO MAINTAIN AN INSPECTION LOG AND TO KEEP RECORDS OF INSPEC- TIONS FOR AT LEAST 3 YEARS AFTER THE DATE OF THE INITIAL INSPECTION, COUNT 6: FAILURE TO DEVELOP AND FOLLOW A WRITTEN SCHEDULE OF INSPECTIONS OF OPERATING EQUIPMENT, SECURITY DEVICES, AND OPERATING AND STRUCTURAL EQUIPMENT USED FOR PREVENTION, DETECTION, OR RESPONSE DETECTION TO HUMAN HEALTH HAZARDS, COUNT 7: FAILURE TO COMPLY WITH TRAINING REQUIREMENTS, COUNT 8: FAILURE TO DEVELOP A WRITTEN CLOSURE PLAN, COUNT 9: FAILURE TO DEMONSTRATE FINANCIAL ASSURANCE FOR CLOSURE, AND COUNT 10: FAILURE TO OBTAIN A WRITTEN TANK INTEGRITY ASSESSMENT. 4. RELIEF SOUGHT PURSUANT TO SECTION 3008 OF RCRA, EPA PRO- POSES A CIVIL PENALTY OF $8,331,500 AND A COMPLIANCE OR- DER REQUIRING THE RESPONDENT TO CORRECT THE VIOLATIONS STATED IN THE COMPLAINT.

1. SECTION 3008(H) OF THE SOLID WASTE DISPOSAL ACT ( RCRA ), AND FURTHER AMENDED BY THE HAZARDOUS AND SOLID WASTE A- MENDMENTS OF 1984, 42 U.S.C. SEC. 6928(H). 2. FORMOSA PLASTICS CORPORATION, TEXAS P.O. BOX 400 POINT COMFORT, TEXAS 77978 FACILITY ID NO. TXT490011293 3. RESPONDENT BEGAN CONSTRUCTION OF THE FACILITY IN JUN., 1980 AND BEGAN OPERATION IN DEC., 1982. PURSUANT TO RCRA SECTION 3010, THE RESPONDENT HAS FILED THE NOTIFICATION REQUIRED OF GENERATORS OF HAZARDOUS WASTE. AS PART OF ITS FACILITY, RESPONDENT OWNS AND OPERATES A WASTEWATER TREATMENT SYSTE. THE SYSTEM IS DESIGNED TO TREAT SPENT PROCESS WATER PRIOR TO DISCHARGE. RESPONDENT HAS NOT OPERATED ITS FACILITY WITHOUT UPSET OR ACCIDENT DURING THE TENURE OF ITS OPERATION AT ITS POINT COMFORT PRODUCTION FACILITY. THERE HAS BEEN A RELEASE OF HAZARDOUS WASTE AND HAZARDOUS WASTE CONSTITUENTS INTO THE ENVIRONMENT FROM THE FACILITY WHICH CONSTITUENTS A POTENTIAL THREAT OF HARM TO HUMAN HEALTH AND THE ENVIRONMENT. 4. RELIEF SOUGHT PURSUANT TO SECTION 3008(H), EPA ISSUED AN ADMINISTRATIVE ORDER ON CONSENT TO THE RESPONDENT. THE INTERIM MEASURES AND COMPREHENSIVE CORRECTIVE ACTIONS RE- QUIRED BY THIS ORDER ARE CONSISTENT WITH RCRA AND ARE NECESSARY TO ACERTAIN THE NATURE AND EXTENT OF THE RE- LEASE AT THE FACILITY, AND ARE NECESSARY TO PROTECT HUMAN HEALTH AND THE ENVIRONMENT. THE RESPONDENT IS ORDERED TO PERFORM THE FOLLOWING ACTIONS: A. CORRECTIVE ACTION 1. ACCELERATED RCRA INVESTIGATION (ARFI) 2. INTERIM MEASURES (IM) 3. RCRA FACILITY INVESTIGATION 4. CORRECTIVE MEASURES STUDY 5. CORRECTIVE MEASURES IMPLEMENTATION (CMI) B. SAMPLING C. REPORTING AND PUBLIC ACCESS TO DOCUMENTS D. FACILITY ACCESS E. RECORD PRESERVATION F. FINANCIAL ASSURANCE G. DISPUTE RESOLUTION H. REIMBURSEMENT OF OVERSIGHT COSTS

Formosa Plastics Corporation, Texas (Formosa) entered into an Administrative Order on Consent (AOC) on February 27, 1991 with EPA for their Point Comfort, TX facility. The AOC is issued pursuant to RCRA Section 3008(h), requiring the facility to conduct corrective actions to remedy an historic release of ethylene dichloride. Formosa will implement interim measures to control groundwater flow, will investigate the nature and extent of the contamination at the facility, and will propose and implement corrective measures, as required under RCRA.

The United States also alleges that Formosa Plastics Corporation, Texas violated CAA provisions regulating benzene waste operations and Emergency Planning and Community Right-to-Know Act (``EPCRA'') toxic release inventory reporting obligations. The alleged violations occurred at co-located facilities in Point Comfort, Texas, owned and operated by Formosa Plastics Corporation, Texas and Formosa Hydrocarbons Company, Inc., and a facility located in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, that is owned and operated by Formosa Plastics Corporation, Louisiana. First Amendment to Consent Decree-WHEREAS, in 2011, pursuant to the reporting requirements of the Consent Decree, FPC TX notified EPA that FPC TX had failed to include in its LDAR program pieces of equipment from a section of the hydrocarbons process unit that should have been included under applicable regulations.

records.caseName: BAYER CROP SCIENCE, L.P. (DELAWARE CITY PVC SITE)
records.description: The Region has approved a CERCLA 104/107/122 settlement under which Stauffer Management Company will perform an RI/FS at the Delaware City PVC Site in New Castle County, Delaware (Site) and reimburse EPA's oversight costs. The Site consists of (1) the parcels of land in located on and near the intersection of Route 13 and Wrangle Hill Road in New Castle County, Delaware, upon which Stauffer Chemical Company (Stauffer) operated a PVC manufacturing plant from approximately 1966 through 1981 and upon which Formosa Plastics Corporation (Formosa) continued manufacturing operations from approximately 1981 through the present (Plant Property); and (2) all locations to which hazardous substances or pollutants and contaminants have migrated from the Plant Property. The Site was listed on the NPL in 1983. EPA issued a ROD in 1986. Stauffer and Formosa implemented remedial action to clean up soils and remediate contaminated groundwater in 1992. Recent investigations have revealed contaminated groundwater beyond the reach of the pump and treat system installed by Stauffer (Site-related contamination is present on the adjacent refinery and in a lower aquifer which was previously believed to not be impacted by the Site). Under the settlement, Stauffer will investigate contaminated groundwater beyond the reach of the existing remediation system.

3/2015-In a settlement with the U.S. and the states of AL and OK, Continental Carbon Co. has agreed to install pollution control technology that will significantly cut emissions of harmful air pollutants at manufacturing facilities in AL, OK and TX, EPA and DOJ announced today. The settlement will resolve claims that Houston-based Continental violated the CAA by modifying their facilities in a way that caused the release of excess SO2 and NOx. The settlement requires Continental to pay a civil penalty of $650,000, which will be shared with AL and OK, co-plaintiffs in the case. Continental must also spend $550,000 on environmental projects to help mitigate the harmful effects of air pollution on the environment and to benefit local communities, including at least $25,000 on energy efficiency projects in the communities near each of the three facilities. ?This settlement brings another major carbon black company into compliance with a law that protects clean air for American communities,? said Cynthia Giles, asst administrator for EPA?s Office of Enforcement and Compliance Assurance. ?By investigating all 15 carbon black manufacturing plants in the U.S., EPA is committed to improving public health and leveling the playing field for companies that follow the law. By installing the latest pollution control technology and funding environmental projects, Continental is taking steps to reduce emissions of air pollutants that can lead to serious health problems.? ?Today?s agreement is good news for residents living near Continental facilities in AL OK, and TX, who will benefit from cleaner air for years to come because of this action,? said Asst Atty General John C. Cruden for the Justice Dept?s Environment and Natural Resources Div. ?The agmt also reflects our continuing efforts to vigorously enforce the CAA to protect public health and the environment. The settlement requires Continental to control large sources of air pollution with advanced technology and requires projects that will have a direct and positive impact on Continental?s neighbors.? Continental manufactures carbon black, a fine carbonaceous powder used in tires, plastics, rubber, inkjet toner and cosmetics, at facilities in Phenix City, AL., Ponca City, OK., and Sunray, TX. Because the oil used to make carbon black is high in sulfur, its production creates large amounts of nitrogen oxide, sulfur dioxide and particulate matter. This settlement supports EPA?s and DOJ's national efforts to advance environmental justice by working to protect communities such as Phenix City and Ponca City that have been disproportionately impacted by pollution. EPA expects that the actions required by the settlement will reduce harmful emissions by approximately 6,278 tons per year of sulfur dioxide and 1,590 tons per year of nitrogen oxide. Continental estimates that it will spend about $98 million to implement the required measures. The pollution reductions will be achieved through the installation, upgrade and operation of state-of-the-art pollution control devices designed to reduce emissions and protect public health. EPA concluded that the modifications made at Continental?s plants violated the Clean Air Act based on information the company submitted in response to an information request from EPA in 2007. EPA issued notices of violation to Continental for these claims in 2012. The settlement was filed with the United States District Court for the Western District Court of Oklahoma and is subject to a 30 day public comment period. The company is required to pay the penalty within 30 days after the court approves the settlement.

records.caseName: Continental Carbon Company-TX OK-CAA Consent Decree (Lead) (National Case)-2015
records.description: On May 7, 2015, a Consent Decree was entered between the United States and the states of Alabama and Oklahoma, and Continental Carbon Company (Continental). Continental has agreed to install pollution control technology that will significantly cut emissions of harmful air pollutants at manufacturing facilities in Alabama, Oklahoma and Texas. The settlement will resolve claims that Continental violated the Clean Air Act by modifying their facilities in a way that caused the release of excess sulfur dioxide (SO2) and nitrogen oxide (NOx). The settlement requires Continental to pay a civil penalty of $650,000, which will be shared with Alabama and Oklahoma, co-plaintiffs in the case. Continental must also spend $550,000 on environmental projects to help mitigate the harmful effects of air pollution on the environment and to benefit local communities, including at least $25,000 on energy efficiency projects in the communities near each of the three facilities. Amendment: Changes the date by which the Wet Gas Scrubber (WGS), which controls sulfur dioxide emissions, and the Selective Catalytic Reduction (SCR), which controls nitrogen oxide emissions, would be installed and operated at Continental's Ponca City, OK, facilities by about 2.5 years later, to April 1, 2021.
